brief:
A filmmaker from Gaza has criticized a film titled NAZA for depicting how genocide unfolds while failing to examine why it occurs, according to the Electronic Intifada. The filmmaker's concern centers on the documentary's approach to representing mass atrocity, arguing that depicting mechanisms of killing without exploring underlying causes presents an incomplete account.

The critique raises questions about how films document conflict and atrocity. The filmmaker's emotional response—captured in the headline's reference to screaming—suggests a personal stakes in how Gaza's experiences are portrayed on screen and the responsibility of filmmakers to provide historical and political context alongside documentation of violence.
dek: Film looks at how genocide is carried out. But fails to look at why.
title: Gaza filmmaker critiques documentary for omitting genocide's causes
